CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the response to the current treatment regimen for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, and to assess any new developments since the last visit.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, expressing a mixed response to the adjustments made during the last visit. He reports that while his anxiety levels have remained relatively stable, he has experienced an increase in irritability, particularly in stressful work situations, which has begun to affect his interpersonal relationships. He remains compliant with his sertraline regimen of 300 mg daily, although he expresses concern over his persistent difficulties with concentration and mood variability.
His tension-type headaches have continued to occur weekly, with a reported intensity of 4 out of 10, which he attributes to ongoing work-related stressors. He notes that the topiramate at 150 mg daily continues to provide some relief, though he has had to occasionally supplement with ibuprofen for breakthrough pain, using it about once every two weeks.
Sleep quality has shown slight improvement, with Mr. Smith reporting an average of 7 to 8 hours of sleep per night. The addition of melatonin at 3 mg nightly has been beneficial in reducing sleep onset latency; however, he still experiences some residual morning drowsiness, which he finds troubling. He has continued to discontinue gabapentin, feeling that it contributed to his daytime fatigue.
Despite these improvements, Mr. Smith reports ongoing fatigue, particularly in the afternoons, which he describes as overwhelming and limiting his productivity both at work and at home. He has continued to engage in physical activity, but he feels that his energy levels do not support his efforts to maintain a consistent routine.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 8. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (added) 9. Gabapentin 200 mg at bedtime (discontinued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to prioritize physical activity, incorporating brisk walks during lunch breaks and weekend hikes. He reports maintaining a balanced diet and has further reduced his caffeine intake. His commitment to mindfulness practices, including meditation and yoga, persists, and he finds these techniques increasingly beneficial for managing his anxiety symptoms. His journaling practice continues to support his self-reflection and emotional regulation.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; increased irritability noted; sleep quality improved; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue reported, particularly in the afternoons, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/76 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears fatigued but engaged; mood appears anxious with mild distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with moderate distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Recommend ongoing cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to further address irritability and concentration challenges. Consider increasing frequency of therapy sessions if symptoms persist. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime and melatonin 3 mg nightly; reassess efficacy and side effects in one month. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain headache diary to monitor frequency and intensity. Consider referral to a neurologist if headaches worsen. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued lifestyle modifications and consider referral to a sleep specialist for further evaluation of potential underlying conditions, including sleep apnea or thyroid dysfunction. Additionally, recommend a thorough evaluation of work-related stressors contributing to fatigue.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-03-23 to assess symptom progression, medication efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain open communication regarding his treatment response and any lifestyle changes he implements.
